# Module DOC — Documents

For repositories that write documents as HTML: reports, notes, papers, pages. Two styles, one for each kind of
reader, carried in this object under `documents/` so that every repository that vendors it has the same two files at
the same hash. A binding that names this module says which of its documents use which style, and which of these rules
it checks.

## The two styles and when to use each

`documents/STYLE.html` is the **engineering** style, for readers on the team: black on white, Georgia, one dense
column, every table ruled. `documents/STYLE-PUBLIC.html` is the **public** style, for readers outside: dark ink and
warm greys, New York and San Francisco, room around everything, figures with colour roles, and mathematics typeset
from LaTeX. Both share one skeleton and one rule, EVERYTHING MUST BE SEMANTIC, stated in the comment in each head.

| Document | Style |
|---|---|
| A report on a piece of work, an experiment's write-up, a `REPORT.html` | STYLE |
| A design note, a review, a runbook, a post-mortem, a status page for the team | STYLE |
| Anything whose reader needs every number and would rather have a table than a sentence | STYLE |
| A paper or preprint, a result written up for people outside the team | STYLE-PUBLIC |
| A project's public page, a note to a customer or collaborator, a page linked from outside | STYLE-PUBLIC |
| Anything a stranger reads first, where one figure has to carry the point | STYLE-PUBLIC |

The test is the reader, not the subject: the same result is a STYLE report while it is being worked on and a
STYLE-PUBLIC page when it is told to someone else. A document that moves outward is re-headed and rewritten for its
new reader, not restyled by hand.

`STYLE.html` is Hestia's `tools/semdoc/STYLE.html` taken byte for byte (SHA-256 `d4ac0a8d…dcda3`, 2026-09-26), so
that `semdoc check`, which compares a document's head with STYLE's exactly, keeps working. `STYLE-PUBLIC.html` is
generated by `documents/build/make_style_public.py`; edit the script, not the page.

## Requirements

**DOC.1 The style is chosen by the reader.** A document for readers on the team uses STYLE; a document for readers
outside it uses STYLE-PUBLIC. The table above gives the common cases; where a document has both readers, it is two
documents.
> *Means* — 4.4, meaning is written for a reader; the two readers need different amounts of it. *Governs* —
> semantics. *CALM* — not applicable. *Checked by* — advice. *Brief* — Engineering reports, experiment write-ups,
> design notes and runbooks use `documents/STYLE.html`; papers, public pages and anything written for readers outside
> the team use `documents/STYLE-PUBLIC.html`. Choose by the reader, not the subject.

**DOC.2 The head is copied whole.** A document's head is its style's head, byte for byte, from the vendored copy: the
semantic rule and, for STYLE-PUBLIC, the colour rule travel in its comment. A change to a style is made in this
object and reaches documents by copying the head again, never by editing one document's style block.
> *Means* — 12.3, a vendored copy is pinned, not edited. *Governs* — state. *CALM* — not applicable. *Checked by* —
> `semdoc check` for STYLE (Hestia `tools/semdoc`); for STYLE-PUBLIC, advice until a checker compares its head.
> *Brief* — Copy the chosen style's head whole from `vendor/code-standard/documents/`; never edit a document's style
> block. Change the style in the object instead.

**DOC.3 Everything is semantic, in one file.** An element is chosen for what the content is; a class names a role,
not a look; no script, no fonts, nothing from the network; every image is inside the file, a raster as a data URI and
a vector as inline svg with a title. The full rule is the comment in the head; this requirement is that it is obeyed.
> *Means* — the head's comment in both styles. *Governs* — semantics, effect. *CALM* — not applicable. *Checked by*
> — `semdoc check` for STYLE; review for STYLE-PUBLIC. *Brief* — Semantic elements only, a class names a role, one
> file with no script, fonts or network; follow the rule in the head's comment.

**DOC.4 A figure's colour does one of two jobs.** In STYLE-PUBLIC a figure that singles out one thing draws it in
blue-700 and everything else in the base greys; a figure that compares several things fills them in the pastels,
blue-200, red-200, yellow-150, cyan-100, in that order, four at most, as fills without outlines. Colour is never the
only cue: the highlighted mark is labelled and compared series are named in a legend. The values are Flexoki's,
exact [Flexoki].
> *Means* — the colour rule in STYLE-PUBLIC's head. *Governs* — semantics. *CALM* — not applicable. *Checked by* —
> review. *Brief* — In a public figure, one accent (blue-700 `#1A4F8C`) to single out one thing, or up to four pastel
> fills (`#92BFDB` `#F89A8A` `#F1D67E` `#BFE8D9`, in order, never outlined) to compare several; label or name every
> coloured mark.

**DOC.5 A figure is centred, and says where it came from.** A figure is centred in the column, and a chart with axes
is centred on its plot area, its viewBox leaving the same gutter on both sides. The caption begins with the figure's
label, says what the image is, and names the source and renderer of anything rendered.
> *Means* — the figure rules in both heads' comments. *Governs* — semantics. *CALM* — not applicable. *Checked by*
> — review; a generator that draws charts through one function that sets the viewBox, as
> `documents/build/make_style_public.py` does. *Brief* — Centre figures, and centre a chart on its plot area, not
> its labels; a caption gives the label, what the image is and where it came from.

**DOC.6 Mathematics is MathML, compiled from LaTeX.** In STYLE-PUBLIC, mathematics is written in LaTeX in the
source and compiled to MathML when the document is built, with Temml at the pinned version [Temml]. It is never an
image of a formula and never script in the page; the only class the compiled MathML may carry is Temml's italic
correction on a superscript.
> *Means* — DOC.3 applied to formulas; MathML is text the browser typesets. *Governs* — semantics, effect. *CALM* —
> not applicable. *Checked by* — the build stops on any other class or inline style in the MathML. *Brief* — Write
> public mathematics in LaTeX and compile it to MathML at build time with the pinned Temml; no images of formulas, no
> script, no maths font files.

**DOC.7 STYLE-PUBLIC is generated.** `documents/STYLE-PUBLIC.html` is written by
`documents/build/make_style_public.py` and is exactly what that script writes: its specimen charts are computed, not
drawn, and its maths is compiled. A change is made in the script and the page regenerated.
> *Means* — 4.2, the page is derived; the script is what is edited. *Governs* — state, transformation. *CALM* — not
> applicable. *Checked by* — `documents/build/make_style_public.py --check`. *Brief* — Change STYLE-PUBLIC in
> `documents/build/make_style_public.py`, regenerate, and run it with `--check`; never edit the page by hand.

<!-- brief: Documents: which style -->
- Team reader (report, write-up, design note, runbook): `vendor/code-standard/documents/STYLE.html`.
- Outside reader (paper, public page, note to a collaborator): `vendor/code-standard/documents/STYLE-PUBLIC.html`.
- Copy the chosen head whole; the rules travel in its comment. Open the file to see a specimen of every element.
